A switch receives a frame whose destination MAC address is not in its MAC address table. What does it do?
B. Sends it back out of the port it arrived on
C. Floods it out of all other ports
D. Sends it to the router
C - unknown unicast frames are flooded out of every port except the incoming one.
Eight PCs connect to one switch (one PC per port), and the switch connects to one router interface. How many broadcast domains exist?
One - a switch does not split broadcast domains. The router interface is in the same one.
Name the two ways a router helps reduce traffic problems on a LAN.
It does not forward broadcasts by default, and it can filter by Layer 3 information. - these are the two advantages the book gives.

The book's Figure 1.5 shows the usual order: Internet  Firewall  Router  Switches  hosts (PCs, printer, server, IP phone, access point). The firewall is the guard between the outside world and your inside network.

Which feature lets an NGFW allow a company app but block a game running on the same port?
B - AVC identifies the application, not only the port number.
In one sentence, what is the difference between an IDS and an IPS?
An IDS only alerts; an IPS sits in the traffic path and can block. - that is the whole idea behind "detection" versus "prevention".

Which IEEE standard is called PoE+ and how much power can the switch port supply?

A company has a small campus and wants to save money while keeping most hierarchy benefits. Which design fits?
D. Hub and spoke with hubs
B - a collapsed core merges the core and distribution layers into one set of switches.
Which statement about a Layer 2 switch is TRUE?
A. It creates one collision domain for all ports
B. It creates one broadcast domain per port
C. It builds its table from source MAC addresses
D. It forwards frames based on IP addresses
C - a switch learns from source MAC addresses. It makes one collision domain per port and does not split broadcast domains.
What does an NGFW inspect that a traditional port-based firewall does not?
Application-layer (Layer 7) content, with application visibility and control and IPS. - that is what makes it "next-generation".
A T1 line is made of how many DS0 channels and what is its speed?
24 DS0 channels, 1.544 Mbps - E1 is the European version with 30 channels and 2.048 Mbps.
Single-mode or multimode: which has the smaller core and goes farther?
Single-mode - the tighter core lets one mode of light travel much farther.
Which standard delivers up to 15.4 W at the port?
B - 802.3af (PoE) gives 15.4 W at the PSE.
An interface shows "up / down". Is this a Layer 1 or Layer 2 problem?
Layer 2 - "up" means a link signal is detected (Layer 1 is fine); "down" protocol means Layer 2 is not working.
Name one cause of late collisions on a switched link.
A duplex mismatch (or a cable that is too long) - late collisions should not happen on a healthy full-duplex switched link.
Switch: Layer 2, reads frame MAC addresses. Router: Layer 3, reads IP addresses in packets and splits broadcast domains.
Hub: 1 collision + 1 broadcast. Switch: 1 collision per port, 1 broadcast. Router: splits broadcast domains.

Core = fast and reliable, no ACLs. Distribution = policy, routing, filtering. Access = connect users, microsegmentation. Layers are logical.
Core and distribution merged. Cheaper, for smaller campuses.
Data centre. Leaf = ToR switch. Every leaf connects to every spine. Spines connect only to leaves. One spine hop between leaves.

Single-mode: tiny core, long distance, costs more. Multimode: larger core, shorter distance. Immune to crosstalk.
